When osq query runs, a manual_edits table lists every manual edit record, listed last after recertifications
When a change is planned, the plan prompt ends with the manual edits whose capabilities no change has written since
When osq's decisions are read, ADR 021 is accepted, and its checks test holds autopilot off by default
When osq.config.ts holds an autopilot block, the loaded config holds enabled, and any other key or value fails loading
When a human runs osq queue approve, osq records every item's hash and clears an autopilot stop, and osq queue shows what the approval covers
When the watcher asks what autopilot does next, osq reads the queue, its approval and the item's change and names one step
When autopilot is on, the watcher plans, approves, runs and lands each approved queue item in order through the command functions, and stops with one record when a step needs a human
When autopilot has stopped, osq inbox and osq status show the reason and the one command that resumes the queue
When the home view lists an autopilot stop, it shows the reason and links the title only when the stop names a change
When a language map reads a Cargo workspace, it lists each crate's test folders, and the Rust adapter finds each test module's lines
When an executor edits a preexisting Rust test in a crate's tests folder or inside a test module without tests.modify, the runner kills the task
When a task's scope holds an existing crate test without tests.modify, lint rejects the task
When osq reports the gates a Rust project lacks, the test-modification gate is no longer one
When osq reads the Rust preset, it names cargo and its subcommands as verify runners, and verify-command lint covers Rust
When a Rust project's task verify runs cargo, lint accepts it, and a chained verify without package.json is told to use a script file
When the Rust adapter reads a Cargo.toml, it returns the crates every dependency table declares, or the line where it could not read
When a task adds a crate to a scoped Cargo.toml, the watcher records it and kills the task when an accepted ADR denies it or the manifest cannot be read
When osq reports the gates a Rust project lacks, the denied-dependency gate is no longer one
When osq-core reads an event line, it yields the typed Event or a read error, and writes it back with the same JSON value
When a change's event streams are folded, task and change state follow the transition tables and the status order
When a change is approved or archived, only a matching seal or a done change passes, and the compiler refuses any other path
When osq's decisions are read, ADRs 022 to 026 are accepted for rust-core with their checks, and nothing warns
When an executor reads AGENTS.md, it finds crates/ in the Layout and a Rust crates section with the rules for working there
When an ADR's applies_to names group:<name>, readDecisions resolves governs to the group's members and validation warns on a group with no living member
When an ADR applies to a group, decisions lint, traceability, the system graph and the ADR docs page treat each member as named
When osq's decisions are read, ADRs 022 to 026 apply to group:rust and still govern rust-core with no warning
When scripts/mutants-rust.sh runs over the workspace, every mutant cargo-mutants makes in rust-core is caught by a test
When Rust CI runs, it checks each push's and pull request's diff with cargo-mutants and the whole workspace weekly, and ADR 024 says the check blocks
When osq runs a verify for a change with a base commit, the command gets OSQ_DIFF naming a file with the change's diff
When scripts/verify-rust.sh runs with OSQ_DIFF set, it runs cargo-mutants on that diff after the tests, and AGENTS.md tells executors so
